content.text: {"id": "mm6215a1", "data_focus": {"v": "yes", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "The overall, annualized age-adjusted traffic-related pedestrian death rate was 1.58 deaths per 100,000 population."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "a total of 47,392 pedestrians (32,873 males and 14,519 females) died from traffic crashes"}]}, "outcome_types": [{"v": "count/rate", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "The age-adjusted death rate for males (2.29) was 2.5 times the rate for females (0.92)."}, {"loc": "table 2", "q": "Annualized death rate (95% CI)"}]}], "analytic_depth": [{"v": "summary", "ev": [{"loc": "summary", "q": "Adults aged ≥75 years and American Indians/Alaska Natives had the highest traffic-related pedestrian death rates in the United States during 2001–2010."}]}, {"v": "comparison", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "The age-adjusted death rate for males (2.29) was 2.5 times the rate for females (0.92)."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "For males aged 75–84 and ≥85 years, Hispanic (11.05 and 14.70, respectively) and A/PI (12.30 and 20.53, respectively) death rates were statistically greater"}]}, {"v": "stratified/adjusted", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "had statistically higher death rates than those in the same age groups at other urbanization levels"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Annualized death rates for sex, race/ethnicity, and urbanization level were age-adjusted to the 2000 standard U.S. population."}]}], "study_design": [{"v": "surveillance/descriptive", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "CDC analyzed 2001–2010 data from the National Vital Statistics System (NVSS)."}]}], "methods_quotes": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Annualized death rates for sex, race/ethnicity, and urbanization level were age-adjusted to the 2000 standard U.S. population."}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Traffic-related pedestrian death counts less than 20 (and the associated rates) were not reported for racial/ethnic populations"}], "confidence": "high", "uncertain_fields": []}
